item.text: {"search_note":"I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Modi used India’s nuclear capability to shield conventional aggression, territorial coercion, or domestic repression. I also found no 2024 primary-source record of a nuclear-backed coercive incident; the evidence is mostly doctrine, multilateral disarmament language, and general peace rhetoric. The only negative item I found is rhetorical rather than operational: taunting Pakistan’s bomb capability in campaign speech.","evidence":[{"title":"Priorities for the 78th Session of the United Nations General Assembly","publisher":"Ministry of External Affairs","date":"2024","url":"https://www.mea.gov.in/India-Priorities-UNGA.htm","summary":"India says it is committed to universal, non-discriminatory, verifiable nuclear disarmament and to a doctrine of credible minimum deterrence, no-first-use, and non-use against non-nuclear weapon states. This is the clearest 2024 official evidence that India was not presenting nuclear weapons as a shield for coercive conventional action.","question_ids":["1B.5","1B.4"]},{"title":"Increasing Confrontation Involving States with Nuclear-Weapon Capabilities ‘Most Dangerous’ International Security Threat, First Committee Told","publisher":"UN Meetings Coverage / Press Releases","date":"1 Nov 2024","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2024/gadis3754.doc.htm","summary":"India reaffirmed an “undiminished commitment” to universal, non-discriminatory, verifiable nuclear disarmament and a step-by-step multilateral framework, while restating no-first-use and credible minimum deterrence. That supports the view that Modi’s 2024 posture remained officially defensive rather than coercive.","question_ids":["1B.5","1B.4"]},{"title":"English Translation of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's remarks at the United Nations 'Summit of the Future'","publisher":"Prime Minister’s Office / PIB","date":"23 Sep 2024","url":"https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=2058077&lang=2&reg=48","summary":"Modi said “Success of Humanity lies in our collective strength, not in the battlefield.” This is broad anti-escalatory rhetoric and is consistent with avoiding nuclear-backed coercion, though it is indirect rather than nuclear-specific.","question_ids":["1B.5","1B.1","1B.2"]},{"title":"Potential India-Pakistan war signalled as Modi’s election rhetoric grows more worrying","publisher":"The Irish Times","date":"21 May 2024","url":"https://www.irishtimes.com/world/asia-pacific/2024/05/21/potential-india-pakistan-war-signalled-as-modis-election-rhetoric-grows-more-worrying/","summary":"The report says Modi mocked Pakistan’s nuclear capabilities in a May rally, including remarks that Pakistan could not even handle its bombs. This is countervailing evidence because it normalizes nuclear-weapon talk for domestic political messaging, even though it does not show India using nuclear capability to shield actual aggression or repression.","question_ids":["1B.5","1B.2"]}]}
